content.body:
WW1 convinced the French military that the 8mm Lebel cartridge needed to be replaced. Many choices were tested, with the final choice being the 7.5 x 55mm MAS round. This testing process and entirely new rifle design meant that the Fusil MAS.36 was the last bolt action rifle adopted by a major army anywhere in the world.
Its receiver was based around a much-modified and shortened Mauser bolt action. Although it was regarded as an ugly and clumsy weapon ... however, it could stand up to virtually any sort of abuse known to man, from surviving explosions to being used as an improvised club or crowbar.
content.brief: Type: Regular Infantry Rifle Caliber: 7.5mm x 55mm Fr.Service Magazine Capacity: 5 rounds Muzzle Velocity: 716 m/s Included weapons: 4 x No.36M HE grenades 4 x M18 smoke grenade 1 x ammo resupply pack 1 x combat knife
